title: The pear cover
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The cover is a pear. Just a pear, on the counter, in the uncle's line of light. The owner asks if it's the uncle. Wood asks how she'd know. She says everyone knows the uncle.

panels.composition: The cover: a pear on a wooden counter in a shaft of light from a small window. Nothing else.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing a single pear on a wooden counter in a shaft of window light, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner with it. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a small booklet and squinting at it while a young man waits, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood, taken aback. The town knows the pear.

image.prompt: a young man taken aback in a laundromat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The digest in the rack. A man in a rain hood at the rack — no. Just a man. Taking one. Looking at the pear. Smiling. Everyone knows the uncle.

image.prompt: a man in a rain hood taking a small booklet from a wire rack and smiling at its cover, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Everyone knows the uncle.' The town reads the pear.
